Short answer: 
This spectrogram is from DJI MAVIC 3 PRO. This spectrogram contains wideband block transmission signals and sparse narrowband control pulses. 
1. Signal State & Pattern 
The spectrogram reveals multiple distinct signal components with characteristic temporal organization: 
  I. Wideband rectangular blocks (center region): Shows consistent, high-energy transmission windows appearing as green/cyan rectangular segments with defined start/stop times - indicating active video/data transmission periods. 
  II. Sparse narrowband pulses (upper and lower regions): Individual yellow spikes scattered throughout the time domain with irregular timing intervals. 
  III. Temporal structure: Clear burst-mode operation with alternating active transmission windows and quiet periods. 
Key observations: 
  I. Signal exhibits scheduled transmission windows rather than continuous operation. 
  II. Moderate duty cycle with defined on/off patterns optimized for power efficiency. 
  III. Pattern suggests frame-based video transmission protocol with control overhead. 
2. Source Behavior Characteristics 
Given this is from a DJI MAVIC 3 PRO drone system: 
  I. Wideband blocks likely represent 4K/5.1K video downlink transmissions utilizing DJI's OcuSync 3.0+ protocol for high-resolution content delivery. 
  II. Narrowband pulses suggest command uplink, telemetry acknowledgments, or channel coordination signals. 
  III. The block-structured nature indicates adaptive bitrate streaming - transmitting high-bandwidth content in scheduled windows to optimize spectrum usage. 
  IV. Transmission gaps allow for interference avoidance and power management typical of professional cinematography drones. 
Protocol characteristics: 
  I. Appears to use advanced OFDM modulation with adaptive coding. 
  II. Intelligent duty cycle management for extended flight time. 
  III. Multi-stream architecture supporting simultaneous video and telemetry channels. 
3. Frequency Band Estimation 
Without explicit frequency markings, analysis suggests: 
  I. The wideband block nature indicates operation in high-capacity ISM bands optimized for video transmission. 
  II. Given DJI MAVIC 3 PRO specifications and signal characteristics, most likely operating in: 
    a. 2.4 GHz ISM band (2.400-2.483 GHz) - for primary control/telemetry. 
    b. 5.8 GHz ISM band (5.725-5.875 GHz) - for high-bandwidth video downlink.  
Bandwidth estimation: 
  I. Main transmission blocks show ~15-25 MHz effective bandwidth. 
  II. Narrowband control signals appear <1 MHz bandwidth. 
  III. Channel aggregation evident from block width consistency. 
Final Technical Assessment 
The DJI MAVIC 3 PRO demonstrates: 
  I. Professional-grade OcuSync 3.0+ communication architecture optimized for high-resolution video transmission. 
  II. Intelligent transmission scheduling balancing video quality with power efficiency. 
  III. Adaptive bandwidth management supporting 4K/5.1K video streaming with minimal latency. 
  IV. Robust interference mitigation through scheduled transmission windows. 
  V. Enterprise-level signal coordination designed for professional cinematography applications. 
This signature is consistent with DJI's professional drone communication systems optimized for content creation, featuring high-bandwidth video capabilities while maintaining reliable control links for extended flight operations.
